newsitem.title: UK: Bid speculation boosts Alliance & Leicester.
newsitem.headline: Bid speculation boosts Alliance & Leicester.

text.p: The share price of Britain's former building society Alliance & Leicester Plc rocketed to 571.5p in early afternoon trade on Monday, its first trading day, compared to an estimate of between 385p and 435p made by the bank's advisers last October.
Banking analysts said bid hopes were helping fuel the market euphoria over the price, that boosted Alliance's value to 3.3 billion pounds ($5.4 billion).
Although Alliance shares had been expected to outperform forecasts because banking shares have risen substantially since October, analysts said the current price was hard to justify on fundamentals.
"Something has to happen to justify this price," said John Leonard, banking analyst at Salomon Brothers.
Leonard said the market was already speculating that a bid for Alliance might emerge -- or that the bank would spend some surplus capital on buying back some shares.
Leonard said he had valued Alliance at between 480 and 500p on fundamentals while another analyst, who declined to be named, had put the bank's value at between 465 and 480p.
Despite fevered speculation that Alliance could be a bid target, analysts say any bidder would have done better launch an offer before the group decided to float.

Under recent legislation, Alliance is protected from takeover for five years unless the bank itself buys another financial institution, or 75 percent of its shareholders decide to give up the immunity.

Both these scenarios are seen as likely by analysts as Alliance has made no secret of the fact that it wants to expand through acquisitions in such areas as insurance, mortgage lending and corporate banking.

"As well as losing protection through buying, if someone comes along with a big enough carrot, the shareholders are likely to take the money especially as the bid would probably be an agreed one," said another analyst.

Also boosting the share price was speculation that Alliance could return some excess capital now that it has floated, but the bank might prefer to spend this on acquisitions which might be less popular with the market.

Share traders were also trying to work out what implications Monday's flotation would have on other building societies coming to market this year which include the largest, Halifax Building Society, and Woolwich Building Society.
"I can't see bid speculation adding much to the valuation of the Halifax," said one analyst, "It's too big already and the Woolwich would also be a big bite for anyone."
The Halifax float will be worth at least 12 billion pounds while, if the Alliance is anything to go by, the Woolwich could have a market capitalisation of at least 4.0 billion pounds.
Other banks were mostly firmer on Monday with the Alliance's most comparable rival Abbey National gaining 9.5p to 808.
"This higher than expected performance from Alliance could help the Abbey but we think the Abbey is a better bet on fundamentals anyway," said one analyst.
The market will now be watching Monday's second auction of shares sold by Alliance members.
The first of these took place on Friday producing bids between 517p and 546p with an average a whisker over 522p.

"That's looking cheap now, so it will be interesting to see if the institutions stand fast or are panicked into getting nearer the current market price which they obviously don't like," said one analyst.
($ = 0.612 British Pounds)
